question.problem:
Given that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{36}∼N(0,{18}^{2})$ is a random sample of size $36$ from a normal population, calculate $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.8).$

*Hint: A value table of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.6026\,$ | $\,0.6064\,$ | $\,0.6103\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6406\,$ | $\,0.6443\,$ | $\,0.6480\,$ |
| $\,0.4\,$ | $\,0.6772\,$ | $\,0.6808\,$ | $\,0.6844\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
If ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a normal population, where 

$$
{X}_{i}∼N(\mu ,{\sigma }^{2}),\,1\le i\le n,
$$

then the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ has the distribution

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

Therefore, the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(0,\frac{{18}^{2}}{36}) \\  & ∼N(0,9).\end{aligned}
$$

We're required to find $P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.8).$

First, we transform $X$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.8) & =1-P(|\overset{―}{X}|<0.8) \\  & =1-P(-0.8<\overset{―}{X}<0.8) \\  & =1-P(\frac{-0.8-0}{\sqrt{9}}<Z<\frac{0.8-0}{\sqrt{9}}) \\  & =1-P(-0.27<Z<0.27) \\  & =1-(Φ(0.27)-Φ(-0.27)) \\  & =1+Φ(-0.27)-Φ(0.27)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.27) & =0.6064,\end{aligned}
$$

and by the symmetry of the normal distribution,

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.27) & =1-Φ(0.27) \\  & =1-0.6064 \\  & =0.3936.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(|\overset{―}{X}|>0.8) & =1+Φ(-0.27)-Φ(0.27) \\  & =1+0.3936-0.6064 \\  & =0.7872.\end{aligned}
$$
